newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan reforms expected to boost stocks.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan reforms expected to boost stocks.

text.p: Constitutional and economic reforms unveiled in Pakistan are likely to attract foreign investment and bring some life to the stock market, analysts said on Wednesday.
Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz on Friday announced the economic reforms that lower corporate, income and sales tax and give incentives to industry to boost production.
Parliament on Tuesday passed landmark constitutional amendments stripping the president of powers to sack governments and appoint armed forces chiefs and provincial governors.
Arif Habib, president of the Karachi Stock Exchange, said the reforms and amendments would mobilise savings, boost exports and would stimulate the capital market.

"The package for the revival of the economy is in a very real sense a package for the revival of the capital market because as the economy grows so will the capital market and as corporate profitability improves so will the returns to the investor," he said.
Former exchange president Yasin Lakhani said the amendments could give much-needed political stability, vital to long-term foreign investment.
"One can hopefully look forward to better days," Lakhani said. "It augurs well. It will give a big boost to the stock market."
"The development will have a major long-term impact on the development of democracy in Pakistan," said an analyst with BMA Capital Management.

"This will also be important for the economic policies that are being formulated by the new government, which can be quite sure of completing its five-year term and hence can afford to address the deep-rooted structural problems in the economy."
Stock prices on Tuesday closed sharply higher on fresh buying by long-term investors. The Karachi bourse 100-share index ended 18.90 points, or 1.20 percent, higher at 1,593.60.
